prs.title: fix: omit version postfix from S2 style macro class names in tests
prs.author: bhovhannes
prs.body:
## Problem

Since #8207, the style macro appends a postfix derived from the `@react-spectrum/s2` version to every generated class name (e.g. `sd171` for 1.7.1). Its purpose is to avoid conflicts between class names of different S2 versions on the same page.

In unit tests this postfix only causes churn: every snapshot containing class names generated by the style macro changes with every S2 release, even when no style changed. This affects S2 itself (the inline snapshots in `style-macro.test.js` are rewritten by every Publish commit, e.g. 4dd44e0f4) and consumers that snapshot components styled with the macro. At Adobe Workfront and GenStudio we currently use a custom mock of the style macro just to strip the postfix in tests.

## Solution

Skip the postfix when `NODE_ENV === 'test'`. Tests don't load CSS of multiple S2 versions into one page, so the conflict the postfix prevents does not apply there. This is consistent with the existing test-specific handling in the macro (calling `style` without `{type: 'macro'}` is allowed when `NODE_ENV === 'test'`). Production and development builds are unaffected.

The rest of the class name is generated from `properties.json` and does not depend on the version (#8118), so with this change class names in tests only change when the style definition changes.

The `style-macro.test.js` snapshots are updated accordingly. The only differences are the removed postfix and the `-macro-static-*` / `-macro-dynamic-*` debug ids, which are hashes o

prs.title: fix(Tree): make TreeItem with hasChildItems expandable without child rows
prs.author: SimenB
prs.body:
Closes #10659

`hasChildItems` on `TreeItem` is documented as "Whether this item has children, even if not loaded yet", but a row with `hasChildItems` and no child rows in the collection cannot be expanded. It gets no `aria-expanded`, and neither the chevron nor `ArrowRight` opens it. The only workaround is to render a `TreeLoadMoreItem` under the row.

`useGridListItem` already reads `hasChildItems` to decide whether a row is expandable, but `TreeItem` never passes it to `useTreeItem`, so the hook falls back to counting child nodes. `TreeItem` now passes `props.hasChildItems` through. Such a row now gets `aria-expanded`, expands and collapses with the chevron and arrow keys, and toggles on row press when the tree has no selection or action.

The v3 and S2 `TreeView` items spread their props onto `TreeItem`, so they pick this up as well. The v3 `TreeView` test for such a row asserted the old behaviour and now expects `aria-expanded="false"`. The matching `TODO` in v3 `TreeView.tsx` is removed.

The new test in `Tree.test.tsx` renders a row with `hasChildItems` and no children, then expands it with a chevron click and with `ArrowRight`.
